title: Chocolate Chip Stuffed French Toast
changes_from_base: A sweet cream cheese and chocolate chip filling is sealed between two slices, dipped in a light egg, flour and water batter and fried until the chips just soften; no cinnamon custard.
summary: Rich chocolate chip cream cheese tucked between crisp fried bread, finished with a maple syrup drizzle.

ingredients.item: slices good white sandwich bread (about 280 g)

steps.title: Stir filling
steps.text: Mix 113 g cream cheese with 1½ tbsp caster sugar and 45 g chocolate chips until the chips are evenly distributed.

steps.title: Close sandwiches
steps.text: Spread the mixture over 4 bread slices and top with the remaining slices, pressing the edges firmly.

steps.title: Thin batter
steps.text: Whisk 1 egg with 240 ml cold water, 65 g plain flour and 1 tsp vanilla in a shallow dish until lump-free.

steps.title: Fry batch one
steps.text: Melt half of the 56 g butter in a large non-stick pan, dip two sandwiches in the batter and fry until the outside is a deep golden brown, about 3 min on each side.

steps.title: Fry batch two
steps.text: Melt the rest of the butter and cook the remaining sandwiches the same way.

steps.title: Cut and serve
steps.text: Slice into triangles and serve immediately with 60 ml maple syrup, while the chocolate is still soft.

tips: The chocolate chips soften as they cook, so handle the hot sandwiches carefully when slicing.
Keep the pan at a steady medium heat so the chocolate melts without the crust burning.
Serve immediately for the best contrast between crisp toast and molten filling.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best served fresh while the chocolate is still soft; store any extra covered in the fridge for a day and warm through before eating. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
